For those looking to read the salary beyond the gross value, the starting point is the combination of G permit, withholding tax and Swiss contributions.
### The professional perimeter
The professional profile and the cross-border profile remain two distinct levels. The editorial outline identifies the possible recognition of the qualification among the requirements, but does not associate an institution, a procedure, a deadline or a figure with this item. The material used here therefore focuses the analysis on tax and contribution treatment; it does not add a salary range or title recognition process.
The G permit belongs to the framework of cross-border work, while the recognition of the qualification is mentioned together with the requirements. This distinction avoids confusing the authorization linked to cross-border work with professional qualification. The territorial reference remains the Canton of Ticino and the employment relationship between Switzerland and Italy, without introducing names of companies, cities or individual cases.
### Tax does not coincide with title
If you are looking for the new 2026 tax agreement, the correct effective date is January 1, 2024, not 2026. The historical reference for double taxation is the Italy-Switzerland Convention signed on March 9, 1976. For the cross-border worker's income from work, the withholding takes place only in Switzerland; Italy avoids double taxation with the tax credit in the EC framework of 730. The same income should therefore not be presented as taxed in both countries.
Furthermore, Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member. The question on the real salary must therefore be read through the contribution items and the documented tax thresholds, without transforming the G permit or professional title into an unreported salary figure. ## Deductibles and tax comparison
The most concrete comparison for a cross-border commuter concerns the tax category in which he falls. The verified facts distinguish those who were already cross-border workers before 17 July 2023 from those who are among the new cross-border workers. The difference concerns the threshold indicated by the regime and must be read together with the period of application.
| Category | Treatment indicated | Period | |---|---|---| | Old cross-border workers | Exemption of €7'500 | Transitional regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border workers | Deductible of €10'000 | New Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 |
### Two categories, two thresholds
For old cross-border workers, the condition referred to is to already be such before 17 July 2023. This category is associated with an exemption of €7,500 in the transitional regime covering the period 2024–2033. For new cross-border commuters, however, the figure indicated is a deductible of €10,000. The table keeps the two items separate because the source assigns them to different categories; they are not presented as cumulative amounts.
This comparison is useful for the work of a social health worker in Ticino because it links the tax calendar to the condition of cross-border worker, but does not replace the pay slip data. The thresholds describe treatment under the tax framework and do not constitute a salary range for OSS. The issue of refunds also remains distinct: the table concerns exemption and deductible, not a salary item.
### Tax at source and IRPEF
The withholding tax on the cross-border worker's income is indicated only in Switzerland. On the Italian side, double taxation is avoided through the tax credit in the EC framework of 730. This is the point not to be confused with the Italian IRPEF rates, which belong to the Italian system and are indicated for different periods.
From 2026, the source reports 23% up to €28,000, 33% between €28,001 and €50,000 and 43% above €50,000, based on Law 199/2025, art. 1 c. 3. For 2024–2025 income, the rates shown are 23%, 35% and 43%. The comparison between these periods does not change the rule according to which, for cross-border workers, the withholding tax on earned income is described as applied only in Switzerland. Instead, it serves to separate the Italian IRPEF regulation from the Swiss withholding tax. ## Contributions, insurance and calculation limits
The Swiss contribution framework allows you to better define which items affect the economic relationship of a border worker, even when a salary amount is not indicated. ### LAMal and rate administration
LAMal means health insurance, not a "health tax". Border workers with a G permit have the right of option. For adults, the deductibles indicated range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. The framework does not report monthly premiums and does not link a deductible to a specific salary as a social health worker.
Tax rates, including source tax and federal or cantonal rates, are set by federal and cantonal laws. At the federal level they are administered by AFC/ESTV and, for the cantonal part, by the cantonal tax administrations. ## TL;DR - Agreement signed on December 23, 2020, in force from January 1, 2024 - Old cross-border workers: exemption of €7'500 in the 2024–2033 period - New cross-border workers: allowance of €10'000
## Key facts - Signing of the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement → December 23, 2020 - Entry into force → January 1, 2024 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of June 13, 2023 - Old cross-border workers → €7'500 exemption, transitional regime 2024–2033 - New cross-border workers → €10'000 allowance
December 23, 2020 is the date the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement was signed; its entry into force is set for January 1, 2024. Italian ratification is Law 83 of June 13, 2023. For anyone seeking vocational training or retraining in 2026 related to work in Canton Ticino, the first fact to focus on is therefore the agreement’s already verified timeline, not a new effective date in 2026.
### The tax framework not to be confused with the course
The expression «new 2026 tax agreement» does not shift these dates. The text distinguishes between old cross-border workers, who already had that status before July 17, 2023, and new cross-border workers. The former are subject to the €7'500 exemption and the transitional regime from 2024 to 2033; for the latter, the stated allowance is €10'000. This distinction is the first documented comparison to keep separate when a family with children assesses whether the retraining is sustainable.
On the cross-border worker’s employment income, withholding tax is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit indicated in box CE of form 730: it is not correct to describe the mechanism as ordinary withholding in both countries. The Italy-Switzerland Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation was signed on March 9, 1976.
Switzerland is not a member of the European Union or the European Economic Area. This is the international framework to bear in mind when discussing cross-border workers and recognition of training, without automatically attributing to a course tax or professional effects that the source does not document. For the holder of a G permit, the insurance aspect remains distinct from that of withholding tax: LAMal is health insurance and not a health tax.
The same verification sequence applies both to those who maintain their current employment relationship and to those considering a change: the thresholds and dates are verifiable data, while the outcome of the course remains to be demonstrated with information not reported here. ## How to compare the practical return
The practical return of retraining is not a number that the source allows to be fixed in the abstract. It is, however, possible to construct an orderly comparison: separate the tax year, the cross-border worker regime, the contribution items, and what the family with children can document. This avoids adding together a tax threshold, an insurance deductible, and financing as if they were the same thing.
The source reports two blocks of Italian IRPEF rates, useful for distinguishing the period before 2026 from the period starting in 2026:
| Period | Italian IRPEF rates | |---|---| | Income 2024–2025 | 23% / 35% / 43% | | From 2026 | 23% up to €28'000; 33% from €28'001 to €50'000; 43% above €50'000 |
The change from 2026 is attributed to Law 199/2025, Article 1, paragraph 3. This information makes it possible to compare two periods, but does not by itself determine the cost of a course or the economic benefit of retraining.
### Two hypothetical scenarios for a family
In a hypothetical scenario, a cross-border worker with children considers a professional development program without assuming a change of employer or income. The comparison then concerns family organization and the economic items actually documented, without attributing an automatic salary increase to attendance.
In a second hypothetical scenario, training is considered for retraining. Here too, the return can be described only through verifiable elements: the reference tax regime, the contributions shown on the payslip, the time devoted, and any financing with documented amount and requirements. The source does not provide a financing amount, so it is not turned into an item in the calculation.
For cross-border workers with a G permit, LAMal concerns health insurance, and the right of option applies. The indicated deductibles for adults range from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. This item should be kept distinct from withholding tax and the return on the course. The same applies to rebates: the material provided does not link them to training and does not offer an amount to include in the family budget.
A cautious checklist can therefore be limited to four fields: tax regime and period, contribution items, any documented financing, and schedules and route compatible with family organization. A possible crossing via Brogeda can be recorded as a logistical question, but the source does not report waiting times, schedules, or costs to turn into a comparison. ## The figures that can be checked
The Swiss part of the comparison is based on contribution items and the payslip, not on generic estimates of a course's returns. In the available framework, AVS/AI/IPG is indicated at 5,3% for the employee. AD/AC is 1,1% with a cap of CHF 148'200. LAINF is indicated between 0,7% and 1,5%, while LPP varies from 7% to 18% by age group starting at age 25.
### Contributions and institutional responsibilities
These values describe the contribution framework that can be used to interpret an employment situation in Ticino, but they do not constitute a budget for a course. It is not correct to automatically add up AVS, LPP, LAMal and withholding tax to obtain the return on retraining: they are different items, and the source does not attribute a specific effect on training to them.
Tax rates, including withholding tax and federal and cantonal rates, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At the federal level, they are administered by AFC/ESTV and, at the cantonal level, by the cantonal tax administrations. UFAS does not set these rates: it is concerned with social security and AVS/AI. BFS collects statistical data and does not set rates.
### What remains outside the verified data
For recognized courses and funding, the source does not list course names, providers, recognition requirements, deadlines or amounts. A faithful article therefore cannot present a specific offering as recognized or funded, nor attribute an already measurable increase in income to retraining.
For a family with children, the practical result is limited: dates, thresholds, rates and contribution items can be laid out; none of this information can be turned into a promise about the course's professional outcome. The same criterion prevents adding amounts not present for refunds, family assistance or commuting. item.title: Death of buffoon pierina: cassan and gallarate investigations
item.description: Friday morning the crash at Cassano Magnago The Jaguar would have been launched at 140 kilometers per hour The Prosecutor evaluates the planning
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Friday morning the crash in Cassano Magnago - The Jaguar would be launched at 140 kilometers per hour - The Prosecutor evaluates the planning of the crime - Night access to Ielmini's house in Gallarate
## Key facts - Investigated → Fulvio Ielmini - Victim → Pierina Buffon - Prosecutor's Office → Busto Arsizio - Crash site → Cassano Magnago - Access to the home → Gallarate - Vehicle → Jaguar - Reported speed → 140 kilometers per hour - Hypothesis → aggravated voluntary homicide and femicide
### The investigation between crash and search for evidence
On Friday morning, in Cassano Magnago, the death of Pierina Buffon was initially linked to the suspicion of road homicide. The reconstruction reported by the source, however, describes a change in direction of the investigation: the investigators are looking for elements compatible with the hypothesis of aggravated voluntary homicide and femicide.
The Busto Arsizio Prosecutor's Office requested documents useful for assessing whether Fulvio Ielmini had planned the action in advance. The point to check also concerns the possible control of the ex-partner's movements and habits. A plan is therefore not indicated as a fact that has already been established: the source explains that this is precisely why further evidence is needed.
During the night between Saturday and Sunday, investigators reached Ielmini's house in Gallarate, concentrating their search on papers, notes, documents and above all computer material. In fact, these supports could contain useful elements to understand whether the man could have monitored Pierina Buffon through GPS devices.
The research therefore includes both paper and IT material: on the one hand notes and documents, on the other tools or information potentially linked to the movements. The source does not report what outcome the investigations had. The sequence connects two places and two levels of the investigation: the reconstruction of the crash is concentrated in Cassano Magnago; in Gallarate the search for traces of previous pipelines.
It is a concrete distinction, because the first step concerns the dynamics of the accident, while the second aims to clarify what could have happened before. The source does not present access as the conclusion of the investigation, but as an activity carried out to seek feedback on the hypothesized planning. ## From the end of the relationship to the GPS devices
### The elements preceding the incident
The part of the investigation concerning the possible planning starts from the end of the relationship between Ielmini and Buffon. According to the text, the man reportedly did not accept the conclusion of the relationship. In the following period, the victim's children allegedly found GPS devices in their mother's car. The source indicates the possibility that these instruments allowed him to monitor the movements of his ex-partner, without reporting what concrete use was actually made of them.
The requested documents, according to the Prosecutor's Office, serve for: > «necessary acts to evaluate whether the suspect proactively planned the action, monitoring the victim's movements and habits».
Alongside the IT material, the reconstruction includes the accounts of the neighbors in Cassano Magnago: they report waiting outside the house, small gifts, and surprises. These behaviors are described as insistent; also for this reason, the woman no longer wanted to humor them and had no intention of resuming the relationship.
The picture also includes two formal initiatives attributed to the victim: a formal warning sent to Ielmini through her lawyer and a police report. According to the investigative reconstruction, not even these steps were enough to stop the reported behaviors.
The significance of these elements lies in their different nature. The GPS devices represent a possible technical trace; the neighbors' accounts describe observed behaviors; the formal warning and the complaint show that the woman had asked to stop the situation also through her lawyer. The source places them in the same investigative framework, but does not attribute definitive proof of planning to any single one of these elements: the question remains the one indicated by the Prosecutor's Office, namely to verify whether the control of movements and habits was part of a previously prepared action. ## The crash and the location of the suspect
### The reconstruction of the collision
According to the first investigations by the local police of Cassano Magnago, Ielmini's Jaguar, a heavy and dated sedan, would have been launched at 140 kilometers per hour against Pierina Buffon's small car. After the lane change, the woman's car would have been hit head-on.
The formulation requires keeping the reported data and its interpretation distinct. The speed, the Jaguar and the change of lane belong to the preliminary findings cited by the source; the hypothesis that the collision was part of an aggravated voluntary action and a femicide is instead the investigative direction that the investigations are trying to verify. The source does not yet present a conclusive decision on this step.
### The wait in the hospital
Ielmini is still guarded at the Varese hospital, where he awaits surgery to reduce the fractures in his leg. The lawyer Angelo Luini describes him as being in a state of confusion. The source thus reports the position of the suspect while he remains under hospital surveillance.
According to Luini, a precautionary measure against the suspect should be formalized in the next few hours. This is an expectation, not an indication that the measure has already been formalized. Furthermore, the source does not report the outcome of the intervention and does not report subsequent developments either on the access to Gallarate's house or on the computer material searched by the investigators.
### The fixed point and the limits of the news
The documented picture remains limited to three elements: the preliminary reconstruction of the crash, the search for any evidence on the planning and the situation of the suspect in the hospital. The first element indicates how the impact would have occurred; the second explains why documents and devices were searched; the third photographs the condition reported in the source.
However, the outcome of the GPS checks, the content of the complaint or warning, nor the decision on the precautionary measure are not reported. Therefore, according to the direction indicated by the Prosecutor's Office, the connections between the previous behaviors, the possible monitoring and the crash in Cassano Magnago remain to be verified. The article documents this phase without transforming the investigative hypotheses into already established facts.

item.description: Two possible demonstrations are reportedly being organized for October 24 One is a student demonstration, with permits in order and peaceful aims
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two possible demonstrations are reportedly in the works for October 24 - One is a student demonstration, with all the proper permits and peaceful aims - The other is associated with fears of vandalism and unrest - At 15:00, Como take on Sassuolo at the Sinigaglia
## Key facts - When → Saturday, October 24 - Location → Como - First initiative → student-led, with all permits in order - Second initiative → event posing a security risk - Match → Como-Sassuolo at 15, Sinigaglia stadium
### Two separate calls
On Saturday, October 24, Como could face two distinct events, organized through online channels and described in opposing terms. Among social media pages and profiles, as well as in specific WhatsApp groups, two events would in fact be in the process of being organized, perhaps not exclusively involving students.
The first call is explicitly student-oriented. The available content describes it as an initiative with all permits in order and entirely peaceful aims, intended to protest against the various problems affecting schools in the city and province.
The second, by contrast, would have objectives much more similar to the vandalism already observed, especially in Milan in recent hours. The report attributes the destruction of shop windows, cars and stores to groups of vandals and hooligans, distinguishing these actions from the peaceful demands expressed in squares and marches.
The material circulated about the second event is limited to just a few messages that were viewed. In one of them, the demonstration is presented as a sort of civil war, with the intention of smashing everything and repeating what happened in Milan. This is the passage referring to the event identified as posing the greatest security risk.
The initial picture is therefore of two events that would have the same date but not the same profile. On the one hand, there is a school protest described as orderly and peaceful; on the other, an event described through messages evoking disorder and damage. The available information does not place the two initiatives on the same footing. ## Fiamma Tricolore's statement
The attention surrounding the potentially riskier demonstration has not remained confined to social media pages. In recent hours, a statement from Marco Dalle, regional secretary of Fiamma Tricolore, reached newsrooms, explicitly mentioning the event scheduled in Como for Saturday, October 24.
The statement opens with events unfolding in Milan and several European cities. Dalle directly addresses the students and young people who will take part in the initiative, reminding them that demonstrating is a fundamental right. According to the statement, however, the right to demonstrate cannot be used as a justification for ravaging, looting, or damaging what people have built through years of sacrifice and work.
Dalle reiterates the message with these words:
Expressing one's dissent remains legitimate, but damage is unacceptable: behind a commercial establishment, a shop window, or any affected property are people, families, and workers who deserve respect.
The appeal therefore concerns not only shop windows or stores, but also the people and families behind the businesses and assets that may be damaged. The position expressed in the statement distinguishes the freedom to protest from acts of destruction and looting.
Dalle then adds an invitation to participants: to bring the Tricolore with them, described as a symbol of national identity and belonging. The message looks to the country's future and emphasizes the need for younger generations to bring Italy, its citizens, everyday difficulties, and their legitimate aspirations back to the forefront.
The statement also addresses solidarity with the people of other countries. For Fiamma Tricolore, this solidarity should not translate into indifference toward the problems experienced daily in Italy. The statement thus adds a public stance to the alert over possible unrest, while the available official confirmations remain few. ## The calendar dilemma
### The Sinigaglia and the deployment of law enforcement
The most delicate part of what follows concerns the schedule already set for Saturday, October 24. At 15 on the same day, Como will host Sassuolo at the Sinigaglia stadium. The match obviously requires a large deployment of law enforcement, an element that makes managing other events in the city over the course of a few hours more complex.
The source specifically points to this overlap of demands. If, in addition to the sporting event, several similar demonstrations were confirmed, it would be difficult to accommodate all the events within the same time period. The difficulty would increase in the case of events scheduled close together or even overlapping.
The sports calendar does not clarify what the outcome of the calls will be, but it introduces a concrete constraint on October 24. On the one hand, there is a home game already listed with its time and stadium; on the other, two possible events are being discussed, with very different characteristics and an uneven level of risk.
At the moment, there is little corroborating information and few official details about the second initiative. The available reconstruction is based mainly on the messages reviewed and on Marco Dalle’s statement, which explicitly referred to fears of new unrest in Como.
The coming hours should provide further information. The main point to clarify concerns the actual scale of the two calls and their compatibility with the event at the Sinigaglia. For now, the coincidence of the match and the possible staging of several demonstrations on the same day leave the mystery surrounding Saturday unresolved.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/como-giallo-su-due-manifestazioni-una-sara-pacifica-nellaltra-vogliono-spaccare-tutto/)*

## TL;DR - A burnout results in Patrick taking a complete leave of absence from work - The policy provides for a limit of 720 or 730 days - The insurer stops payments after a few weeks - The transitional period is generally between three and five months
## Key facts - Persona → Patrick, fictitious name, 55 years old - Inability → complete, certified by his attending physician - Benefits → daily allowances from the employer's sickness insurance - Decision → resumption of the same activity with another employer - Policy limit → 720 or 730 days - Transitional period → as a rule, three to five months
Patrick, a fictitious name, is 55 years old and turned to the trade union over a problem related to his employment relationship. After suffering burnout, he was forced to take leave for treatment and rest. His attending physician certified that he was completely unable to work.
During his absence, he regularly received the daily allowances provided for by the employer's sickness insurance. Once the period of protection shielding the employee from dismissal had elapsed, however, his employer notified him of the termination of his employment.
The dismissal came as a complete shock. At least on the face of it, one certainty remained: if the insurance requirements continued to be met, the allowances would be paid up to the maximum limit provided for by the policy, indicated as 720 or 730 days. One month after the dismissal, however, a new communication arrived. The same insurer announced that payments would stop after a few weeks.
The reason lay in the opinion of the insurer's doctor, according to whom Patrick was able to perform the same activity for another employer. The insurer therefore concluded that he was fit for work again. The decision immediately raised a question, however: can a person who is still ill be expected to find new employment within a few weeks? The answer is no, at least not automatically.
### The principle invoked by the Federal Supreme Court
Under Swiss law, the employee must mitigate the damage and, when the conditions allow, make use of their remaining ability to work. This obligation, however, cannot be assessed in the abstract. The insured person's specific situation must be considered, taking into account their age, health, education and training, professional background and the concrete prospects of reintegration into the labour market.
In the case described, Patrick was 55 years old, had gained experience mainly in the same sector and had medical documentation indicating that he was still completely unable to work. For these reasons, an immediate change was unrealistic. The Federal Supreme Court clarified that, when the insurer invites someone to change employers in order to fulfil the obligation to mitigate the damage, an adequate transitional period must be granted. This allows the person to adapt to the new situation and genuinely seek new employment. As a rule, case law places this period between three and five months, depending on the circumstances of the specific case.
The duration is therefore not separate from the insured person's personal situation. Age, health, education and training, experience and actual prospects of reintegration all help determine whether the time granted is adequate. ## The assessment must remain concrete
The point is not to categorically deny the duty to mitigate the loss. The source acknowledges it, but ties it to a condition: when circumstances allow, the worker must make use of the residual work capacity. This wording prevents the possibility of changing employers from being treated as an automatic process.
| Point | Interpretation consistent with the source | |---|---| | Residual capacity | It must be assessed together with the state of health and medical documentation | | New employer | The search must be concrete, not merely hypothetical | | Transitional period | As a rule, it must fall between three and five months, depending on the case |
The difference is between being able to envisage an activity and being genuinely able to resume it. An insurer may consider that the same job is theoretically available with another employer. Swiss law, however, requires that conclusion to be assessed in relation to the insured person: age, training, professional experience, health, and actual prospects of reintegration must be taken into account in the assessment.
### What this means for cross-border workers
For a cross-border worker who finds themselves in a similar situation, the practical issue concerns the relationship with the employer's sickness insurance, rather than a general rule on every aspect of cross-border work. If the worker is asked to look for a new job while on sick leave, the key issue is whether the request genuinely takes the individual situation into account and allows the time indicated by case law.
Patrick's case shows why the factors should not be considered in isolation. His age of 55, his experience concentrated in the same sector, and his complete incapacity for work, as shown by the medical documentation, combined to make an immediate change unrealistic. It does not follow that everyone is automatically entitled to the upper limit of the range. The duration must be determined on the basis of the concrete circumstances.
The timing distinction also matters. A notice period of a few weeks is not equivalent to the transitional period indicated by the Federal Supreme Court when the insurer asks the worker to change employers. For this reason, the communication must be read not only for its outcome, but also for the time granted and the medical reasoning supporting it. The assessment concerns not only the termination of the contract: it concerns the real possibility of adapting, seeking a new job, and using the residual capacity when conditions allow.
The principle does not eliminate the need to mitigate the loss, but it prevents that requirement from being applied without considering the person and the labor market into which they would have to reintegrate. This is the difference between a theoretical request and a request assessed in the specific case. ## From notification to protection
When the insurance company announces the termination of benefits with short notice, the sequence indicated by the source is actionable and should not be postponed. The worker can act on two fronts: challenge the decision and protect themselves from the risk of being left without income while waiting for a response.
### Five steps to take
1. Do not simply accept the notification. The termination of benefits must be challenged promptly, especially when the notice granted is only a few weeks.
2. Ask for the decision to be reassessed. The request must refer to the insured person's specific situation and not merely to the theoretical possibility of carrying out the same activity for another employer.
3. Provide the available medical documentation. In the case described, complete incapacity certified by the attending physician is an element that must be considered when assessing work capacity.
4. Check the transitional period granted. It is necessary to verify whether the time assigned genuinely allows the person to adapt to the new situation and concretely seek new employment, taking into account age, health, training and professional experience.
5. As a precautionary measure, it is advisable to register in parallel with the regional employment office, that is, for unemployment. This measure aims to avoid being left without income if the insurance company delays its response.
These steps do not replace an assessment of the case. They serve to ensure that a communication affecting daily allowances does not go unanswered and to keep open the review of the insurance requirements, medical documentation and transition period.
For a cross-border worker in a similar situation, the practical advice remains the same: act quickly when the insurance company interrupts benefits and do not confuse registering for unemployment with accepting the decision. The source identifies the trade union or a legal adviser as contacts to involve without delay.
A timely review makes it possible to identify the necessary steps and prevent the passage of time from compromising the possibility of asserting the principles established by law. For the precautionary step related to unemployment, consult disoccupazione frontalieri.

For a cross-border family facing the birth of a child in 2026, the date is the first point to set: the new 2026 tax agreement does not coincide with the year of entry into force. The editorial checklist dedicated to birth revolves around three practices: registry registration, family allowances and consular procedures. The practical simulation should therefore be read as a comparison between three strands, not as a single calculation. The birth date opens the administrative verification; work in the Canton of Ticino must instead be read within its tax and social security framework. ### The cross-border worker's tax framework The rule indicated for earned income is clear: for cross-border workers, withholding tax is only withheld in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the EC 730 framework. The checklist must therefore not transform the income into a double tax, nor present Switzerland as part of the EU or EEA: Switzerland is not an EU/EEA member. The Italy-Switzerland Double Taxation Convention was signed on 9 March 1976. It is the date to be associated with the bilateral framework, while the New Cross-Border Agreement has a distinct sequence: signature on 23 December 2020, Italian ratification with Law 83 of 13 June 2023, which entered into force on 1 January 2024. For the worker with G permit, the KVG chapter remains that of health insurance and includes the right of option for cross-border commuters G. The deductibles for adults indicated by the source range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. The reference is separate from the registry registration, but belongs to the administrative map that a border family may wish to keep tidy in 2026. The practical news, therefore, is not a new rate linked to birth. It is the need not to confuse registry, checks and consulate with withholding tax, double taxation and KVG. To simulate the case without adding amounts not provided, the most robust comparison starts with the worker's category. In the proposed comparison, the criterion is the date on which the worker was already a cross-border commuter. ### The comparison between old and new cross-border commuters | Scenario | Source criterion | Tax data | |---|---|---| | Old cross-border commuter | already one before July 17, 2023 | €7'500 exemption; transitional regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border commuter | new cross-border commuter | €10'000 tax-free allowance | The table serves to distinguish two tax scenarios. It is not a table of family allowances and does not automatically assign an amount to the child. For the birth-related procedure, the three indicated items still need to be kept open: civil registration, family allowances and consular procedures. The second comparison concerns how income is interpreted. Withholding tax remains Swiss only; for Italy, the indicated step is the tax credit in section CE of the 730. This is the point to check when a simulation presents the income of a cross-border commuter from Canton Ticino: the aim is to avoid double taxation, not to add two withholdings. ### Rates and contributions to be kept separate The source indicates three brackets for Italian IRPEF from 2026: 23% up to €28'000, 33% from €28'001 to €50'000 and 43% over €50'000. For 2024–2025, it instead reports 23%, 35% and 43%. These data should be read as the Italian IRPEF framework, distinct from the Swiss withholding described above. On the Swiss side, AVS/AI/IPG is 5.3% for the employee; AD/AC is 1.1% with a cap at CHF 148'200; LAINF is indicated as between 0.7% and 1.5%; LPP ranges from 7% to 18% by age bracket, starting at age 25. These are contribution and pension items, not family allowances. The respective federal and cantonal laws define the tax rates; administration is handled by AFC/ESTV at federal level and by the cantonal tax administrations at cantonal level. UFAS deals with social security, while BFS collects statistical data: neither of the two sets the rates. Distinguishing these responsibilities helps avoid errors in the practical simulation. The operational checklist can be completed in five steps, using only the entries and references from the simulation. ### Five steps for 2026 1. Open three separate sections: civil registry registration, family allowances, consular procedures. These are the three chapters indicated for the birth of a child in a cross-border worker's family. Do not combine them into a single generic item, because the comparison must show which procedure is being examined. 2. Establish the worker's status: G permit and tax category. If the cross-border worker already had that status before July 17, 2023, note the scenario with an exemption of €7'500 and transitional regime 2024–2033. If they fall among the new cross-border workers, note the tax-free allowance of €10'000. The distinction precedes the calculation. 3. For employment income, record only one withholding: withholding tax in Switzerland. In the Italian step, enter the tax credit from section CE of the 730, so that the simulation represents the double-taxation rule without turning it into a levy in both countries. 4. Keep the healthcare and social security portion in a separate box. LAMal means health insurance; G cross-border workers have the right of choice, and the adult deductibles indicated are CHF 300–2'500. In the same check, you can report AVS/AI/IPG at 5.3%, AD/AC at 1.1% up to the cap of CHF 148'200, LAINF between 0.7% and 1.5%, and LPP between 7% and 18% from age 25, by age bracket. 5. Verify the correct tax reference: federal and cantonal rates depend on federal and cantonal laws; at the federal level, the administration is AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations also operate. Do not assign this task to UFAS or BFS. For the Italian part, section CE of the 730 is the point cited by the source. item.description: On the night of October 16–17, another door was broken down The same couple was identified and reported again The large courtyard houses 18 apartments

## TL;DR - Another door was broken through during the night of October 16–17 - The same couple was identified and reported again - The large courtyard houses 18 public housing apartments - Fifteen apartments are currently uninhabitable
## Key facts - Place → Lissago, in the «large courtyard» - When → night between Friday, October 16, and Saturday, October 17 - Involved → same couple already flagged, reported and removed - Outcome → identification and a new report on Saturday morning, October 17 - Structure → 18 apartments used as public housing - Uninhabitable → 15 apartments - First course of action → evictions and sealing - Second course of action → funds from a regional grant to renovate the courtyard
### New episode in Lissago During the night between Friday, October 16, and Saturday, October 17, another door in the «large courtyard» in Lissago was broken down. The same couple, already flagged, reported and removed, entered the apartment. On the morning of Saturday, October 17, State Police officers identified the two occupants and reported them again.
The new report comes as the issue is being addressed on several fronts. Municipal council committees are meeting, the issue is being discussed, local police and State Police are deploying officers and filing reports. Social services are also taking action to try to reach those responsible. Despite this sequence of interventions, the occupations in the courtyard are not stopping.
The «large courtyard» comprises 18 apartments used as public housing. The text describes a vicious circle: a door is forced open, occupants enter, identification and a report follow, but the problem resurfaces. The repetition of the occupations keeps the issue open for those living in the area and for the administrations called upon to manage it.
The Municipality has identified two courses of action and a third, more complex one, for which it nevertheless intends to try every possible avenue.
### Evictions, renovation and assistance The first course of action concerns evictions and sealing. Some occupied apartments have already been subjected to them; the same measures should also be extended to the new homes where the «squatters» have broken down the doors.
The second involves renovating the courtyard. The aim is to obtain funding from a regional grant program to make the 15 apartments currently uninhabitable available, the ones that are systematically occupied. Repopulating the courtyard, according to the approach indicated by the Municipality, would help prevent new occupations and the public-order and hygiene problems connected to the situation.
The third course of action combines the reports, which have now been repeated for weeks, with an attempt to reach the two occupants and bring them back into the network of people assisted by social services. This path is made difficult by the occupants’ own opposition, as they have been known for years to those who provide assistance in the city.
Meanwhile, Lissago residents continue to keep watch and report the new occupations. Their expectation is that a definitive solution will be found, one capable of restoring peace to the nights and dignity to the neighborhood. For a cross-border worker reading the news from the Canton of Ticino, the first practical point is also the article's limitation: the source describes a local news story in Lissago and not a change in the rules governing cross-border employment. It does not attribute to the case any effects on the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, or withholding tax. It does not mention Brogeda, INPS, the new 2026 tax agreement, or double taxation. Presenting a consequence on these issues would mean adding a connection that the text does not provide.
The point that emerges instead concerns the way the Municipality is trying to interrupt a recurring problem. The three lines of action do not have the same target: one concerns apartments already occupied, one the condition of the courtyard, and one the people involved.
### Three directions, three different levels | Direction | Stated objective | Characteristic in the text | |---|---|---| | Evictions and seals | Apply the measures to occupied homes | First route, already under way in some apartments | | Regional call for proposals | Make 15 uninhabitable apartments available and repopulate the courtyard | Longer route, potentially more effective | | Complaints and social services | Repeat the complaints and try to reintegrate the two occupants into the assistance system | Third route, more complex |
The difference is also temporal. Evictions and seals address the newly forced-open doors and occupied apartments. Renovating the courtyard, on the other hand, requires obtaining funding from a regional call for proposals and aims to make the housing units currently uninhabitable usable. The Municipality considers it a longer route, but potentially more effective precisely because it aims to repopulate the complex.
The third line of action concerns the relationship with the two occupants. Complaints have been repeated for weeks, while social services are trying to reach them to bring them back into the support system. The text does, however, point to their opposition, which makes this path more difficult.
For residents, the role described by the source remains one of monitoring and reporting. For institutions, the task is divided among police interventions, municipal decisions, and efforts by social services. The source does not give a date for a definitive solution and does not describe a conclusive outcome of the three paths. The text does not specify a form, a specific office, a telephone number, or a deadline for reports. Therefore, a credible procedure must remain within the steps described by the source, without adding administrative instructions that are not present.
### The sequence described by the source 1. Local monitoring. The residents of Lissago continue to monitor the situation in the courtyard and keep an eye out for new occupations. This is the first step indicated by the text, together with reporting incidents that recur.
2. Reporting. When a new occupation is detected, the residents report it. The source links this activity to the new broken-down door and the subsequent identification of the couple who had already been reported, formally reported to the authorities, and removed.
3. Identification and reporting. In the incident on 17 October, State Police officers identified the occupants and reported them again. The text also recalls that local police and State Police are already engaged, with patrols and reports.
4. Eviction and sealing. The first course indicated by the Municipality consists of evictions and the application of seals. Some occupied apartments have already received them; the Municipality plans to apply them to the new dwellings with broken-down doors as well.
5. Work on the courtyard and assistance. The second course is seeking funding from a regional grant program to renovate the 15 uninhabitable apartments. At the same time, social services are trying to bring the two occupants back into the care system.
These steps do not constitute a guaranteed timeline. The source still speaks of a vicious circle and reports that the occupations have not stopped. Therefore, it is not possible to indicate a closing date for the matter, nor to claim that one of the three courses has already produced a definitive solution. For cross-border commuters, the article does not describe consequences for routes, border crossings, wages, or tax procedures: the concrete information remains the account of events in the courtyard and the activities of residents, the Municipality, the police, and social services.

item.description: In the Mendrisiotto, grape harvesting is set at 15 francs an hour The entry fee is set at up to 4mila francs For unemployed cross-border workers, 900
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Mendrisiotto, the grape harvest is listed at 15 francs an hour - The entry tax is listed at up to 4 thousand francs - For unemployed cross-border workers, 900 million a year is mentioned - 120 million at risk for border municipalities
## Key facts - Location → Mendrisiotto hills - Compensation → 15 francs an hour - Entry tax → up to 4 thousand francs for workers and self-employed people - Allowance → 900 million francs a year - Interministerial roundtable → September 17 - Average salary → 5500 francs more in one year, heading toward 100 thousand
15 francs an hour in the Mendrisiotto hills: the grape harvest opens the sequence of headlines dedicated to cross-border workers. It is the most precise figure on employment, while the other news broadens the picture to taxes, rebates, incomes and unemployment.
One headline mentions an entry tax of up to 4 thousand francs for workers and self-employed people and leaves open the question of who should pay it. Another presents a tax bonus for those who spend in Ticino as an anti-cross-border-shopping idea. The headline does not indicate a bonus amount or the conditions for obtaining it: the discernible point is the idea.
The figure of 900 million recurs in two headlines linked to unemployed cross-border workers. On the one hand, there is the allowance to be paid by Switzerland, with the possibility that Switzerland may say no; on the other, there is talk of a vote against 900 million a year. The sequence signals a financial dispute, but does not provide a breakdown for each individual cross-border worker.
### Rebates, health tax and data
September 17 is associated with the interministerial roundtable on the health tax, double taxation and status. Another headline announces the signed decree on funds from Italy and Switzerland intended for border municipalities and asks who is entitled to the resources. The figure of 120 million appears instead in a headline about municipalities on the border with Switzerland.
The health-tax dossier is presented through opposing positions: there is talk of retaliation by Switzerland against Regione Lombardia, of a halt to the rebates, deemed by the Swiss government to be a violation of the agreements, and of a threat by Ticino to block the rebates. A summit in Bern is scheduled for Thursday. After 912 days, Italian and Swiss trade unions maintain that the levy is a tax, not a contribution.
The concluding section addresses data and incomes: among the topics mentioned are the 5500-franc increase over one year in the average salary in Switzerland, now heading toward 100 thousand, and the disclosure, through pre-filled tax returns, of data on salaries considered protected, involving a breach of privacy and compensation payments. For old cross-border workers, an error concerning data and taxes, an Irpef warning and the transmission of those data for the first time are also reported. Overall, the source juxtaposes employment, taxation and rebates without adding procedural details. ### Different figures, not a single measure
For a cross-border worker, the practical reading starts with separating the figures. The headlines place side by side amounts concerning work, the entry tax, unemployment, municipalities and incomes. They are not presented as a single measure and should not be added together.
| Topic | Wording in the headlines | Cautious reading | |---|---|---| | Grape harvest | 15 francs an hour | hills of Mendrisiotto | | Entry tax | up to 4 thousand francs | employees and self-employed workers | | Unemployed cross-border workers | 900 million a year | benefits paid by Switzerland | | Border municipalities | 120 million at risk | municipalities bordering Switzerland | | Average salary | 5500 francs more in one year | towards 100 thousand |
The comparison shows why an economic headline cannot automatically be turned into a personal calculation. The 15 francs an hour belong to the grape-harvest story; the 4 thousand francs are the limit indicated for the entry tax; the 900 million appear in the story of benefits for unemployed cross-border workers. The 120 million concern the border municipalities, while the 5500 francs refer to the average salary in Switzerland. The source does not link these amounts to one another.
### The wording indicates the status of the news
The verbs also require attention. The entry tax surfaces, the tax bonus is an idea, Switzerland says no and votes against the 900 million, the decree for the border municipalities is signed, and Ticino threatens to block the rebates. Alongside these formulations appear an interministerial roundtable and a summit in Bern. Reading every headline as a definitive decision would add a step that the list does not contain.
As for the health tax, the positions do not coincide. One headline speaks of retaliation by Switzerland against Regione Lombardia; another attributes to the Swiss government the assessment that stopping the rebates is a violation of the agreements; yet another reports Ticino's threat. The Italian and Swiss trade unions, after 912 days, instead maintain that it is a tax and not a contribution. Double taxation appears among the topics of the September 17 roundtable, not as an announced outcome.
The same criterion applies to old cross-border workers and salary data. The headlines juxtapose pre-filled income declarations, privacy, compensation, errors involving data and taxes, and an Irpef alert, but do not turn them into a single procedure. Separating each issue is the only way not to confuse a figure on average income, a dispute over the rebates, and a news report about protected data. ### A five-step check
Anyone following the news roundup can turn the headlines into a structured record, without attributing to the source details it does not contain.
1. Separate the subject. Put the grape harvest in the hills of Mendrisiotto in one entry, the entry tax for workers and self-employed people in another, and the tax bonus for those who spend in Ticino in a third. They are three different headlines, and the bonus continues to be presented as an idea to deter shopping by cross-border workers.
2. Transcribe amounts and units exactly as they appear. Note 15 francs an hour, up to 4 thousand francs, 900 million a year, 120 million at risk and 5500 francs more in a year. Next to the last figure, note the wording toward 100 thousand; next to the 900 million, note the compensation borne by Switzerland and the vote against reported in another headline.
3. Classify the action described. “emerges” and “idea” indicate the wording used for the entry tax and bonus; “says no” and “votes against” concern the 900 million; “signed” refers to the decree on money for border municipalities; “threatens” refers to the blocking of the rebates. The September 17 roundtable and the summit in Bern on Thursday should be recorded as events indicated by the headlines, not as results.
4. Keep the health tax, double taxation, status and rebates separate. For each, associate the positions reported: the Swiss government, Italian and Swiss trade unions, Ticino and Regione Lombardia. The source shows statements and disagreements, but does not provide a single procedure for the cross-border worker.
5. If the reference is to old cross-border workers, create a separate record for data, taxes and Irpef. Include the pre-filled income figures, the transmission of the data for the first time, the privacy warning and compensation. Do not automatically combine these elements with the news item about the average salary in Switzerland.
The final check is simple: every number must remain close to the subject of the headline it comes from and every position must remain attributed to the indicated subject. To turn the tax part into a personal simulation, use the calcolatore fiscale
